claims.title: Model-informed oracle cost is coordinatewise nonincreasing under active-experiment menu expansion
claims.scope: finite active fixed-model problems with a baseline experiment menu literally contained in an enriched menu
assumptions: the enriched singleton-model oracle may ignore all newly added experiments
model identity, horizon, coding universe, and cost accounting are otherwise unchanged
nonclaims: the oracle improvement need not be strict
the theorem does not compare different model families

claims.title: Active-experiment menu expansion cannot worsen deterministic or public-mixed controller value when the regret benchmark is held fixed
claims.scope: baseline and enriched finite active fixed-model policy classes evaluated against the same enriched model-oracle vector
assumptions: every baseline experiment remains available in the enriched menu
public mixing uses the same source-independent assistance model on both sides
nonclaims: own-oracle regret need not be monotone because its benchmark moves
the public-mixed statement treats shared randomness as an explicit resource

claims.title: Own-oracle regret shift is bounded by oracle-improvement extrema minus fixed-benchmark controller gain
claims.scope: finite baseline/enriched active experiment menus with modelwise oracle-improvement vector delta
assumptions: delta_m equals baseline oracle value minus enriched oracle value
fixed-benchmark controller gain is measured against the enriched oracle vector
nonclaims: nonuniform oracle shifts need not yield a scalar equality
the bound does not claim the same worst model before and after expansion

claims.title: A uniform oracle shift gives an exact own-regret identity
claims.scope: baseline/enriched active experiment menus whose model-informed oracle values all improve by the same rational amount d
assumptions: the controller gain is measured with the enriched benchmark fixed
the baseline policy class is contained in the enriched class
nonclaims: the identity does not imply regret is monotone
the result is relative to the declared model-informed causal oracle

claims.title: Minimax own-oracle regret can increase under a strictly richer active-experiment menu
claims.scope: finite active fixed-model decision problems where menu expansion can improve the model-informed oracle more than the shared controller
assumptions: regret is recomputed against each menu's own model-informed oracle
the new experiments remain optional for the shared controller
nonclaims: absolute robust cost cannot increase under the same menu expansion
the theorem does not say regret is an invalid metric; it says benchmark movement matters

claims.title: Specialized K4 sensing leaves robust cost at two while doubling deterministic own-oracle regret from one-half to one
claims.scope: two disjoint-support two-hidden-state K4 models, one no-signal baseline experiment, and two symmetric model-specialized hidden-state experiments
assumptions: each specialized experiment perfectly reveals hidden state under its target model and emits a fair hidden-state-independent coin under the other model
nonclaims: the numerical values are specific to the declared finite K4 construction

claims.title: Public mixing softens but does not remove the specialized K4 moving-benchmark regret increase
claims.scope: the same specialized K4 menu-expansion instance after an independent public seed convexifies complete deterministic policy trees
assumptions: the baseline mixed own-regret is one-half
the enriched fixed-benchmark mixed controller gain is one-quarter
the oracle shift is uniformly one-half
nonclaims: public mixing is an explicit assistance resource
the mixed value three-quarters is not a deterministic policy value

claims.title: When a K3 public-coin menu expansion leaves oracle values unchanged, deterministic own-oracle regret falls exactly by the fixed-benchmark controller gain
claims.scope: one-period point-mass K3 with baseline no signal and an added source-independent uniform three-way public signal
assumptions: all model-informed oracle values remain one
the public signal arrives before deterministic code selection
nonclaims: the regret decrease is coordination value rather than model information

claims.title: Bounded exact active-experiment menu-regret audit
claims.scope: uniform-shift K4, nonuniform-shift K4, zero-shift K3, deterministic and public-mixed fixed-benchmark comparisons, and literal menu-inclusion validation
assumptions: all active policy frontiers, singleton oracles, and public-mixed zero-sum games complete below configured caps
all probabilities and costs use exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded checks are not a continuous-model or scalability theorem
CI success is not empirical evidence for simulation
